theme: Bidders who want bundles or nothing
title: Bidders Who Want Bundles or Nothing
seed_problem: combinatorial-auction winner determination: bundle bids over items with a supply limit, maximize accepted revenue subject to per-item capacity
mutation: composite: layers a genuine bundle-vs-parts complementarity trap (a large bundle bid competing against a spoiler singleton plus fillers on its own items), a weighted-matching trap (a 3-edge path whose priciest middle edge blocks two disjoint cheaper edges worth more together), and uniform-weight odd conflict rings (the classical set-packing LP integrality-gap witness, LP=1.5x integral optimum) into one winner-determination instance, all interleaved with a general overlapping-bundle background under multi-unit item supply; the item-sharing graph decomposes into disjoint small gadget components plus one loose background component, which is exactly what a decompose-then-branch-where-tight solver can exploit and a flat density-greedy cannot see.
strategies: trivial: order-of-arrival greedy (accept each bid, in input order, iff it still fits) -- reproduces the checker's own baseline B exactly

naive greedy: sort all bids by price-per-item density and accept greedily -- systematically prefers the hub-spoiler over the bundle it blocks and the path's priciest middle edge over the two cheaper ends it blocks, in every gadget

insight (strong): union-find the item-sharing graph into connected components; the gadgets are always small isolated components (by construction) -- brute-force each exactly (this is where a fractional relaxation would be loose and would need branching), and handle the one large loose background component with density-greedy plus a bounded local-exchange improvement pass
invalid: accepts every bid regardless of shared-item capacity, guaranteed to oversubscribe every gadget's scarce items -- scores 0
